To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new method is able to describe nuclear structure properties of the $\ensuremath{\text{sd}}$-shell in a systematic and accurate manner.

we developed a new approach for the calculation of energy eigenvalues of the nuclear shell model Hamiltonian in the $\mathrm{\text{sd}}$ shell, that it works well, and that it can be used for the calculation of the energy spectrum for a wide range of nuclei in this shell.

a systematic numerical study of the nuclear structure model developed by us, which is based on the diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in symmetry-projected quasidegenerate HFB vacuum and quasiparticle excitation spaces, shows good agreement with the exact diagonalization of the shell model and a considerable improvement over a previous approach, which is based upon symmetry-projected quasinucleon vacuum and quasineutron/quasiproton excitations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient numerical approach to the nuclear shell model.
the numerical implementation of the multiconfiguration approach and its application to the $\mathrm{A}=20,24,28,30$ nuclei.
the development and application of a new approach for the calculation of energy levels and electromagnetic transition rates in nuclei.

the new model, which is a promising candidate for large scale nuclear shell model studies in the $\mathrm{s}\ensuremath{-}d$ shell region and beyond, has been successfully established.
the present approach is a good candidate for the description of nuclear structure in the $\mathrm {sd}$ shell.
the present approach, although it is not the best possible, is the best possible approach that can be used in practice.
